players.product: KEYTRUDA (pembrolizumab) anti-PD-1 therapy; intismeran autogene (V940/mRNA-4157), jointly developed with Moderna

quarterly_data.quarter: Merck & Co. press release: European Commission Approves KEYTRUDA (pembrolizumab) Plus (10-21-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: The European Commission approved KEYTRUDA (including KEYTRUDA SC, known as KEYTRUDA QLEX in the U.S.) with Padcev (enfortumab vedotin) as neoadjuvant and then adjuvant treatment after radical cystectomy for adults with resectable muscle-invasive bladder cancer, based on the Phase 3 KEYNOTE-B15 trial (run with Pfizer and Astellas), following the CHMP's positive opinion in September 2026. Merck says it is the first and only PD-1 inhibitor plus ADC regimen in the EU for MIBC regardless of cisplatin eligibility, broadening the cisplatin-ineligible approval of less than six months earlier; the authorization covers all 27 EU member states plus Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway, with commercial availability depending on national reimbursement.
quarterly_data.figure: approval in 27 EU member states plus Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway
